co_grocery_store_walls_the.blurb: A cluster of short walls inside Castlewood Canyon State Park south of Denver, popular because the walk from the car is so brief. Most of the climbing is easy to top-rope, with a good share of traditional crack lines and a few bolted routes such as Bozo No No (5.11a, sport). Grades run broadly from the easy fives through the low 5.11s, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.11 range, so it suits beginners, instructors and anyone setting up ropes for a mixed party. Several spots allow a scramble to the top for anchoring. Expect company on weekends.
co_grocery_store_walls_the.parking_note: Come in by the park's west entrance and stop at the first lot beyond the Homestead lot. A trail heads west from there to the base of the walls.
co_grocery_store_walls_the.approach: A short trail west from the parking lot reaches the base of the walls in roughly five minutes.

co_pup_tent_of_solitude.blurb: A small south-facing crag in Main Elk Creek, tucked beneath the larger Fortress of Solitude above Glenwood Springs. Nearly all of it is bolted face and arete climbing, with a handful of trad lines, and the routes are well protected. Grades are spread across the 5.10s, 5.11s and 5.12s, with a smaller group of easier routes in the 5.7 to 5.9 range; Subpar (5.10a, sport) and Toxic Asset (5.10c, sport) are friendly starting points. Sun reaches the wall, so winter days can be pleasant while summer afternoons run warm. The walk in is moderate and short enough to make it an easy half-day stop.
co_pup_tent_of_solitude.approach: A trail climbs from the Hadley Gulch trailhead, and the cliff comes into view across a gulch. Walk to the far right end of the crag, where a climbers' path angles onto the base. Allow about 20 minutes.
co_pup_tent_of_solitude.parking_note: Drive up Main Elk Creek on County Road 243 past the bridge and continue a short way to a small pullout marked by a bighorn sheep sign and an information board. That is the Hadley Gulch trailhead.

co_ruckman_cave.blurb: One of the busiest zones in Rifle Mountain Park, a steep limestone wall with a big roof in its middle. Everything here is bolted: routes either end beneath the roof, pull through it, or climb the overhanging ground on either side. The climbing is powerful and pumpy, with natural pinches and pockets, and the grades cluster hard, mostly 5.12 with a good number of 5.13s, plus a few easier warm-ups to the right. Pinch Fest (5.12b, sport) and Beer Run (5.13a, sport) are the standouts. The cave catches morning sun, which helps on cold days but means evenings suit hot ones better.
co_ruckman_cave.parking_note: A pullout about 1.3 miles up the canyon holds roughly eight cars and sits directly opposite the Meat Wall.
co_ruckman_cave.approach: Cross the plank bridge from the pullout and follow a short path of a few paces to the base, which leads straight to Pinch Fest.

co_tanner_dome.blurb: A granite dome in the Wet Mountains above Oak Creek Canyon near Canon City, with one- to three-pitch routes that are mostly bolted and a few traditional lines. The rock is sound and slabby with some texture, and the bolting ranges from generous to a touch sporty, so a 60 m rope is handy. Grades run mostly 5.8 to 5.11, with a few harder lines such as Rebel Yell (5.12a, sport) and good moderates like Amp Right (5.8+, sport). Many routes are sheltered and pleasant on cold days, while hot afternoons can be punishing, so start early in summer.
co_tanner_dome.parking_note: Take the Oak Creek Grade Road (Fremont County 143) south from Canon City to mile marker 11, where the trailhead parking is.
co_tanner_dome.approach: Hike trail 1333 for about an eighth of a mile, then branch right on a side trail that heads north toward the rock and swings east to the dome. Expect a walk of 20 minutes or more.

co_cloud_shadow.blurb: One of the best-known bouldering zones on Flagstaff Mountain above Boulder. The long wall holds a wide spread of problems from the easiest grades to V12 and beyond, with plenty in the V3 to V7 range, and many are traverses on pebbles, pinches, sloping rails and undercling pockets. Cloud Shadow Traverse (V4+), Stranger Than Friction (V6) and Trice (V12) are among the best. The wall faces southeast and takes afternoon sun, so it is warm in cool weather and often crowded after midday; mornings are quieter.
co_cloud_shadow.parking_note: Park at a roadside pullout on the left of Flagstaff Road, about 1.2 miles above the bridge at Capstan Rock.
co_cloud_shadow.approach: From the pullout, walk uphill about 50 yards to a guardrail at a hairpin bend, step over it and drop southeast to the wall.

co_lower_peanuts.blurb: The lower of two small crags on the north side of Eldorado Canyon, mostly traditional routes of one to three pitches with a few bolted lines. Grades span the 5.6s to the 5.13s, but the bulk fall in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a handful of moderates like Peanuts (5.9+, trad) and West Crack (aka Star Wars) (5.8, trad). The wall stays shaded, a relief in summer heat. It feels remote and gets few visitors; some rock is loose, so a helmet is wise. Descent is by rappel or a walk-off to the climber's right.
co_lower_peanuts.parking_note: Use the parking at the western end of the canyon road, near the Rattlesnake Gulch trailhead.
co_lower_peanuts.approach: Follow the nearly flat Fowler Trail east for about a quarter mile, then scramble up the talus field, hopping boulders, to the base.

co_work_and_play_area.blurb: A mid-grade bouldering zone on the east side of Alderfer/Three Sisters Park near Evergreen, set among boulders in a shady pine forest. It offers a friendly mix of moderates, mostly V0 to V5, with a few harder problems such as The Piano (V8) alongside the lower-grade favorites Guiding Light A.K.A Round Up (V3) and The Troll Cave (V3). The setting is quiet compared with busier Front Range bouldering. Shade keeps it comfortable into summer, and spring and fall are the best seasons for friction. Bring pads.
co_work_and_play_area.parking_note: Use the first, smaller lot on the east side of the park. It fills on busy weekends, and the larger field lot is a ten to fifteen minute walk beyond.
co_work_and_play_area.approach: A flat trail leads into the forest from the first east lot.
